ref: DAR — Revelation ch. 20: The First and Second Resurrections
title: The First and Second Resurrections
voicePrompt: In your own words, walk through Smith's millennium: who the binding angel is and why it is not Christ, what the bottomless pit and the binding of Satan really mean, how the two resurrections frame the thousand years, and what finally happens to the wicked, the earth, and Satan at the great white throne.

questions.stem: Why does Smith conclude that the angel who binds Satan in verse 1 is NOT Christ?
options: Because the angel uses a literal key and chain, which Christ would never need
Because the typical day of atonement shows Satan is the antitypical scape-goat, sent away by another person, not by the High Priest himself
Because Christ remains in heaven during the entire thousand years and never returns to earth
Because the angel comes down from heaven, and Christ ascends rather than descends
questions.explanation: Smith argues from the day-of-atonement type that Satan is the antitypical scape-goat. As the scape-goat was sent away "by the hand of a fit man" — not by the High Priest — so the Devil is sent into the bottomless pit "not by the hand of the High Priest, but by the hand of another person, according to the type. Hence this angel is not Christ."

questions.stem: What does Smith say the "bottomless pit" into which Satan is cast actually is?
options: A literal underground cavern at the center of the earth
The grave, where Satan lies dead during the thousand years
The earth itself, returned to a desolate, chaotic state of darkness and death, as the same Hebrew word describes the 'deep' in Genesis 1:2
A distant region of outer space where Satan is confined among other worlds
questions.explanation: Smith notes the original word signifies an abyss or deep, and that the word rendered "deep" in Genesis 1:2 ("darkness was upon the face of the deep") is the same word. He concludes it denotes the earth brought back to its chaotic state — "a vast charnel-house of desolation and death" — where Satan is confined for a thousand years amid the ruins.

questions.stem: According to Smith, what does the "binding" of Satan for a thousand years actually mean?
options: He is bound with literal chains so he cannot move at all
He is annihilated and ceases to exist until the thousand years end
His subjects are placed beyond his reach — the saints in heaven and the wicked in their graves — so he is confined to a desolate earth in hopeless inactivity
He is imprisoned in heaven where Christ keeps watch over him
questions.explanation: Smith explains that Satan must have subjects to work upon; during the thousand years the saints are in heaven and the wicked are in their graves, so "the 'binding' of Satan means simply the placing beyond his reach of the subjects upon whom he works." He is confined to this earth, condemned to "a state of hopeless inactivity," no longer able to traverse space or visit other worlds.

questions.stem: How does Smith use the phrase "But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished" (verse 5)?
options: He concedes it is an interpolation and drops it from his argument
As the plainest proof of two resurrections — the righteous at the start of the thousand years, the wicked at the end
As proof that all the dead, righteous and wicked, are raised together at one time
As evidence that only the martyrs are ever resurrected
questions.explanation: Smith says "no language could more plainly prove two resurrections; the first, a resurrection of the righteous at the commencement of the thousand years; and the second, that of the wicked at the end of that period." He defends the verse against the charge of interpolation, noting all scholarship is against that claim and the Revised Version retains it.

questions.stem: Through his grammatical argument on the word "which" (hostis) in verse 4, what does Smith establish about those reigning with Christ?
options: That only the beheaded martyrs reign with Christ, and no one else
That the entire human race, including heathen who never heard of the beast, reigns with Christ
That two distinct classes are in view — the beheaded martyrs AND a separate class who had not worshiped the beast or its image
That the beast-worshipers are also raised to reign for a thousand years
questions.explanation: Smith argues the word rendered "which" is the compound relative hostis (not the simple relative hos), introducing "another class." Thus John saw the martyrs as one class and "those who had not worshiped the beast and his image" as another. He adds this does not include the heathen, since the previous chapter shows the wicked were all slain and sealed in death for the thousand years.

questions.stem: Smith rejects the view that the earth is renewed at the second coming and inhabited during the millennium. What is his chief objection to that view?
options: It would require the saints to remain on earth instead of going to heaven, contradicting John's vision of thrones
It would make the resurrected wicked, with the Devil at their head, tread with unhallowed feet on the purified, holy earth, forcing the saints to yield ground and flee into the city
It would mean the thousand years are literal rather than symbolic
It would place the New Jerusalem in Palestine rather than in heaven
questions.explanation: Smith objects that this view "makes the wicked, in their resurrection, come up, with the Devil at their head, and tread with their unhallowed feet upon the purified and holy earth," while the saints who held it for a thousand years "are obliged to yield the ground, and flee into the city." He cannot believe the saints' inheritance would be so marred, and finds no scripture to support it.

questions.stem: How does Smith argue that more than the Devil alone is "tormented day and night" in verse 10?
options: He claims the Greek manuscripts add the names of the wicked dead
He points out the verb "shall be tormented" is plural and agrees with the beast and false prophet, so it cannot refer to the Devil alone
He insists the torment is eternal conscious suffering for all the lost
He argues the saints also pass through the lake of fire unharmed
questions.explanation: Smith notes that "the verb 'shall be tormented' is in the plural, and agrees with the beast and false prophet; whereas it would be in the singular number if it referred to the Devil alone." He explains the beast and false prophet (cast in at the start of the thousand years, Rev. 19:20) refer to the individuals composing those organizations, who come up in the second resurrection as Gog and Magog.

questions.stem: At the great white throne, what does Smith say happens to the earth when it is described as fleeing away so that "no place" is found for it?
options: It is permanently destroyed and the redeemed live forever in heaven instead
It is left a frozen, lifeless rock orbiting the sun
Heated to extreme intensity it is converted to gas and becomes invisible, then the purged elements recombine into a new world for the saved
It is swallowed by the bottomless pit along with Satan
questions.explanation: Smith describes a three-stage burning: the works and wicked are consumed, the globe is fused into a molten mass on which the city floats, and finally the heat reduces the whole earth to gas so it "flee[s] away." But the elements are not destroyed — they are "purged from the last and minutest taint of sin," then recombine as God says "Behold I make all things new," forming the new earth, the everlasting home of the saved.
